notes.subject: car
notes.text: All images come from a Generation 2 camera, mostly sunny despite the island's position.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Long white front and yellow rear plates, with a red coat of arms at left and a letter J starting unblurred codes; no blue strip.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Traffic drives on the left, with signs, chevrons and warnings like the United Kingdom's.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Most street and place names contain words from the language of nearby France, and a local language shows up on some signs.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Pastel walls and dark slate roofs like northern France, plus some terraced houses.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Red granite is a popular material for walls and houses all over the island.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Telephone booths are yellow rather than red.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Cornish palms with thin trunks and arching leaves are common decorative plants.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Yellow give-way lines at junctions, where the United Kingdom uses white double dotted lines.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Cycling signs mention the start or end of a Green Lane; blue route markers have an island map in the centre.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Winding hedged lanes, often tree-covered, like country roads of the United Kingdom.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Most street signs carry the coat of arms of their parish.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: The area around the capital is more urban: taller buildings and narrower streets.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: A vast treeless nature reserve on the west coast, with a gentle westward slope and often overcast skies.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: A greenish-purple discolouration glitch appears in the southwest.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: The only divided road runs along the south coast west of the capital, with a maroon median.
